title: One model, three solvers, one answer

blocks.text: A water authority renews its pipes district by district, and any number of kilometres can be renewed, fractions included. Its analysts are moving the model from one solver to another and want a check that runs in their test suite: the same model on GLOP, HiGHS and PDLP, and a verdict on whether the three answers agree.

Each `District` has a value and a cost per kilometre (both in $k), crew hours per kilometre, a most it may renew and a least a regulator has ordered (`min_km`, 0 when there is no order). With $`D`$ the districts, $`B`$ the budget and $`H`$ the crew hours:

items: `solve_on(districts, budget, hours, solver)` builds this model, solves it with the given `mathopt.SolverType`, and returns the objective value when the status is `OPTIMAL`, otherwise `None`.
`all_agree(values, tol=1e-6)` takes a dict from solver name to value (or `None`) and returns `True` only when every solver returned a value and every pair has a relative gap of at most `tol`.

blocks.text: Exact equality is the wrong test: PDLP stops as soon as its answer is within its tolerance, so its objective may differ from a simplex solver's in the seventh significant digit.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from renewal import District, all_agree, relative_gap, solve_on

towns = [District("Ashby", 8, 5, 2, 9), District("Brook", 6, 2, 3, 10), District("Cleve", 4, 1, 1, 15)]

values = {s.name: solve_on(towns, 50, 35, s)
          for s in (mathopt.SolverType.GLOP, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, mathopt.SolverType.PDLP)}
for name, value in values.items():
    print(f"{name} at budget 50, hours 35:", value if value is None else round(value, 6))
print("all agree within 1e-4:", all_agree(values, 1e-4))
print("gap between 500.0 and 500.2:", round(relative_gap(500.0, 500.2), 6))

def solve_on(districts: list[District], budget: float, hours: float, solver: mathopt.SolverType) -> float | None:
    """Build the renewal LP, solve it with `solver`, and return its objective, or None if not OPTIMAL."""

    return 0.0


def relative_gap(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    """|a - b| measured against the larger magnitude, and never against less than 1."""
    # TODO
    return 1.0


def all_agree(values: dict[str, float | None], tol: float = 1e-6) -> bool:
    """True when every solver returned a value and every pair is within `tol` relative gap."""
    # TODO: a missing value is a disagreement; otherwise compare every pair with relative_gap.
    return False


if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo = [District("North", 9, 4, 2, 10), District("South", 7, 3, 3, 8), District("East", 5, 2, 1, 12)]
    values = {s.name: solve_on(demo, 40, 30, s)
              for s in (mathopt.SolverType.GLOP, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, mathopt.SolverType.PDLP)}
    print(values, all_agree(values))

cases.says: GLOP, HiGHS and PDLP each return the LP's optimum, PDLP within its looser tolerance
the three values agree, and a 1% difference does not
a difference of 1 on an objective of two million is within 1e-6
two objectives near zero are compared against 1, not against their own tiny size
an infeasible model gives None from every solver, and a missing value means the solvers do not agree

origin.section: Same Model, Three Solvers: Compare Objectives With a Relative Tolerance

concepts: the same LP solved on GLOP, HiGHS and PDLP gives objectives that agree within a relative tolerance, not exactly
a solve that ends without OPTIMAL has no objective to compare
